question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Queen Elizabeth I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **East India Company** was granted a charter by **Queen Elizabeth I** in **1600.**
 
• This charter gave the company a monopoly on **English trade with the East Indies**, which included modern-day** India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Indonesia.**
 
• The East India Company played a significant role in **British colonialism and imperialism, **establishing trade relationships and political control over large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Queen Elizabeth I's charter for the East India Company was a key moment in the history of **British imperialism and global trade**, paving the way for centuries of British economic and political influence in Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Edward VI **(reigned 1547-1553) was the **son of Henry VIII **and ruled England for a brief period before his death at the age of 15.
 
• **King Henry IV **(reigned 1399-1413) was the** first monarch **of the House of Lancaster and played a key role in the** English civil war **known as the **Wars of the Roses.**
 
• **Queen Victoria** (reigned 1837-1901) oversaw the height of the **British Empire's global power and influence**, but her reign came long after the **East India Company **had been dissolved and replaced by the British Raj in India.
 
• The **East India Company **was a joint-stock company that was founded in** 1600 and dissolved in 1874,** after centuries of trade and political control in India and other parts of Asia.
